title: Data Visualization Analyst
body: the nisc iv program at leidos has an opening for a data visualization analyst with prior faa or federal experience. the ideal candidate will have a strong background in power bi, powerapps, and power automate to graphically display relevant data for analysis. specific duties for the position include: data analysis and metrics conduct quantitative and qualitative data analysis to identify trends, risks, and opportunities. develop and maintain performance metrics to track progress, compliance, and outcomes for faa programs and offices. provide data-driven recommendations to support strategic decision-making and performance improvement. ensure accuracy, integrity, and reliability of data used for analysis and reporting. dashboards and visualization design and develop visually appealing and intuitive dashboards, reports, and interactive visualizations to present complex data in a clear and concise manner. use data visualization tools such as power bi, tableau, or qlikview to create interactive and user-friendly reports. collaborate with cross-functional teams to identify requirements and design solutions that communicate key insights effectively. stay current with best practices in dashboard development and visualization to enhance usability and accessibility. continuous improvement and knowledge management research industry and other federal agency best practices and provide recommendations for improving program management, data analysis, and reporting practices. identify opportunities to streamline processes, improve data accuracy, and enhance efficiency using fundamental principles of lean, six sigma, and theory of constraints. document lessons learned, processes, and standard operating procedures to support organizational knowledge retention. collaborate with management and stakeholders to understand their needs and translate them into actionable visualization projects. use knowledge, skills, and abilities of a wide variety of advanced computer technologies and theories. maintain an understanding of operations to identify data sources by owner, as well as presentation needs. additional responsibilities may include: program and project management support program and project planning, execution, monitoring, and reporting using scope, schedule, and cost management tools. develop and maintain integrated project schedules, milestones, and deliverables in alignment with faa requirements. track and report risks, issues, and dependencies, and recommend mitigation strategies. prepare executive-level project briefings, decision memos, and reports that clearly communicate program status, risks, and recommendations. technical writing and executive briefings develop, review, and edit technical documentation, project reports, and executive correspondence to ensure accuracy and clarity. create high-quality executive-level presentations and briefing materials for senior leadership, including complex data reporting. maintain consistency of style and messaging across all program and project deliverables. data analysis and metrics basic qualifications: ba degree and 8+ years of prior relevant experience or masters with 6+ years of prior relevant experience. will consider equivalent relevant experience in lieu of a degree. ability to obtain a public trust clearance. proficiency in using ms office (word, powerpoint, excel) alteryx, power bi, tableau, powerapps, and power automate to design dashboards, automate workflows, and present analytical data. demonstrated experience in data analysis, statistical monitoring and reporting. strong technical writing skills, with ability to draft clear, concise and accurate reports and presentations. proven ability to produce and communicate high quality executive presentations and communications, including drafting reports, memos, or responses for senior leadership and external stakeholders. excellent verbal communication skills. able to provide data efficiently and effectively to stakeholders with high quality and integrity. strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to anticipate issues and propose solutions. experience with microsoft office. optimistic attitude, poise, and team player. preferred qualifications: experience with federal hr management and compliance frameworks, including opm. dot, faa policies and programs. experience supporting large-scale program management office efforts. previous government contracting work experience. working knowledge of sharepoint. project management certification (e.g., pmp) to demonstrate formal training in managing scope, schedule, and cost. knowledge of data governance, quality assurance, and security practices to ensure compliance with federal standards. ability to perform advanced statistical analysis and modeling using tools such as python, or sas. experience in developing and maintaining standard operating procedures (sops), playbooks, and knowledge management repositories. stakeholder engagement and facilitation skills, including the ability to support cross-functional workshops and collaborative planning sessions. title: Lead Substation Engineer - Technical Project Lead
body: leidos engineering has an opportunity for a lead substation engineer – technical project lead. leidos is seeking an experienced substation engineering leader to serve as the technical lead for complex high-voltage and ehv substation epc projects. in this role, you will own the overall technical delivery of projects from conceptual design through detailed engineering, procurement, construction support, and energization. you will lead multidisciplinary engineering teams spanning substation physical, protection and control, scada/communications, relay settings, civil/structural, and related disciplines. you are not expected to be the subject-matter expert performing every discipline's detailed design; rather, you will provide the technical leadership, engineering judgment, coordination, and oversight necessary to deliver an integrated, constructible substation design. this position will be part of our unique and fast-growing epc solutions group, which sits within our power delivery solutions division that provides consulting services to both public-owned and investor-owned electric utilities. these consulting services provide clients with overall project management tasks in the areas of comprehensive engineering design of electrical transmission and distribution, substation and transmission line projects nationwide. as a lead substation engineer – technical project lead, you can expect to: serve as the overall technical lead for hv and ehv substation epc projects, with responsibility for the integrated technical solution and engineering deliverables. lead multidisciplinary engineering teams including substation physical, protection and control, relay settings, scada/communications, civil, structural, geotechnical, and other supporting disciplines . establish the project's technical approach, design basis, engineering execution strategy, and interdisciplinary requirements. provide technical leadership and ownership of substation physical and protection & control design, making and driving key technical decisions, resolving design issues, and ensuring an integrated, constructible solution across all engineering disciplines. coordinate technical interfaces between engineering disciplines, equipment suppliers, construction teams, clients, and project management. identify and resolve cross-discipline design issues and make or facilitate key technical decisions affecting safety, constructability, cost, schedule, quality, and performance. oversee engineering from conceptual design and scope development through ifc design, procurement, construction support, testing/commissioning, and energization. serve as a primary technical point of contact with the client and communicate technical recommendations, risks, alternatives, and decisions. lead technical reviews and ensure appropriate qa/qc is performed across the engineering package. mentor engineers and develop future project technical leads. understand and apply industry standards, applicable state and federal safety codes, regulatory compliance requirements, and construction codes to projects. create equipment, material, construction, and testing and commissioning specifications. perform quality control (qc) reviews and lead qc review meetings on applicable engineering deliverables produced by junior staff, peers, and remote offices on small, medium, and large projects while adhering to the pds quality management standard. provide technical oversight, direction, and support for project teams. assure proper documentation of project technical data. coordinate with project managers to successfully deliver projects to our clients. work directly with clients on project-related issues. direct and/or participate in client meetings and job-site visits to collect and deliver design and engineering information. identify and resolve project-related issues while proactively communicating and collaborating with the client. perform evaluations of existing facilities to propose upgrades and replacements and present findings and recommendations to our clients. apply value engineering principals for economized, constructible, and safe designs. complete conceptual design (one-line and general layout) to support project planning. provide professional mentorship while setting and maintaining a positive professional example for the team and junior staff what sets you apart (background qualifications): bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering from an accredited university with eight (8) + years of prior relevant experience in utility substation design/engineering; professional engineer (pe) license required demonstrated experience serving as a lead engineer, project engineer, technical lead, or engineering manager for hv/ehv substation projects. demonstrated ability to lead multidisciplinary engineering teams and coordinate interfaces among substation physical, p&c, scada/communications, civil/structural, and other disciplines. strong working knowledge of both substation physical and p&c design, with technical depth in at least one substation discipline. comprehensive understanding of the utility grid (power generation, transmission, and distribution) system and the theories and principles involved in substation engineering. comprehensive understanding of industry standards (including nec, nesc, nema, ieee/ansi) and their application to projects. competence in researching engineering and design issues, evaluating alternatives, making sound recommendations, and preparing and presenting recommendations. ability to meet deadlines under high-pressure situations. high level of computer competency/proficiency with using ms office applications. team player who can work effectively in a team environment with an ability to deal with and lead a variety of individuals from various socio-economic, cultural, and ethnic backgrounds. strong written and oral communication skills; strong organizational skills. ability to travel locally/regionally up to 15% of the time you might also have (preferred qualifications): hv/ehv project experience brownfield and greenfield substation experience experience working on epc or progressive design build contracts experience with serving as firm-client liaison in a support and lead engineering role. prior experience as a substation lead engineer performing qc reviews and staff training/mentorship experience leading renewable generation projects or interconnections experience with engineering programs and software (including skm, aspen, etap, cdegs, or vendor software). active membership in national engineering societies and work groups (ieee, pes, etc.) construction support experience. at leidos, we pride ourselves on being a trusted and technology-focused solutions provider. our power delivery services team is the go-to for utilities and mobile operators who need reliable power and telecommunication expertise. we've worked with over 50 investor-owned utilities, over 160 municipals/cooperatives, and we're continuing to expand our reach. plus, we've got an amazing group of industry-leading construction partners who help us deliver meaningful energy delivery solutions. our recognition as an industry leader has been confirmed time and time again. engineering news-record (enr) has ranked leidos among the top 10 t&d firms and top 10 power firms. pdspm pdssubstation if you're looking for comfort, keep scrolling. at leidos, we outthink, outbuild, and outpace the status quo — because the title: Senior Subcontracts Specialist
body: leidos is an innovation company rapidly addressing the world's most vexing challenges in national security and health. our global supply chain organization is seeking a senior subcontracts specialist to support the programs, proposals, and business objectives of the defense sector. this role will lead full life cycle (“cradle-to-grave”) subcontract management activities supporting primarily us government programs which complies with contract requirements, company policies and procedures, and applicable laws and acquisition regulations. this role will support the airborne & mission solutions business area which supports programs and proposal opportunities that deliver smart, integrated, mission-ready solutions that enhance military intelligence operations and accelerate decision advantage for the warfighter. we achieve this through advanced platform and systems integration, rapid systems modernization, repeatable mission software offerings, and intelligence and data rationalization that turns information into actionable insight. the successful candidate will be the primary interface between subcontractors and the program for the contractual management of agreements of various types typically of a moderate dollar value, risk, creativity and complexity, and will interact with other functional areas (e.g., program management, contracts, project control, finance, growth, etc.) to complete the necessary activities for the portfolio they’re assigned. they will provide strategic proposal support centered around the win strategy and be expected to effectively manage their time, prioritize actions, meet deadlines with minimal supervision, and be a detail-oriented peer who can work both independently and as part of a team. primary responsibilities the position requires an advanced knowledge of federal subcontracting and experience providing creative solutions to business and program requirements. while not an exhaustive list, activities in the subcontracting process that are responsibilities of this role are: supporting proposal activities (e.g., negotiation of non-disclosure agreements (ndas) and teaming agreements, preparation of complex solicitation packages from customer requirements, evaluation of subcontractor proposals, price analysis, negotiation of scope, price, and terms and conditions, etc.), subcontract award, and post-award management (e.g., subcontract modifications, risk identification & mitigation , issue resolution, internal reporting, closeout activities, etc.). the complexity of assignments will increase with demonstrated proficiency, judgement, and business acumen. accordingly, the candidate will be expected to identify and resolve moderately complex issues and problems on assigned subcontracts and make recommendations of appropriate mitigation steps to management. the candidate may assist management by reviewing files for compliance and coaching more junior staff on policies, procedures, and best practices. basic qualifications typically requires a bachelor’s degree and 4 - 8 years of prior relevant experience or master’s with 2 - 6 years of prior relevant experience. must be us citizen. experience awarding and managing subcontracts in a government approved purchasing system including an intermediate knowledge of the requirements of the far and dfars experience negotiating price and complex terms and conditions must have the organizational skills to manage concurrent projects and possess the business acumen to appropriately prioritize actions and deal effectively with subcontract management issues of varying degrees of complexity through resolution. must be able to clearly articulate statuses and issues to management, internal partners, and suppliers preferred qualifications undergraduate degree preference: supply chain management or business administration working experience with automated purchasing system (preferably deltek costpoint and ivalua) experience independently leading the subcontracts portion of proposal efforts experience building strong supplier relationships that can be leveraged to assist in future issue resolution title: Technical Development Lead - Real-Time Visibility
body: the leidos digital modernization sector has a career opportunity for a technical development lead - real-time visibility supporting the global solutions management - operations ii (gsm-o ii) contract with the defense information systems agency (disa). the gsm-o ii program supports the operations, sustainment, maintenance, repair, and defense of the defense information system network (disn) within the dod information network (dodin), as well as mission modernization efforts that improve operational effectiveness, resiliency, and service delivery for disa and its mission partners. the rtv technical lead will serve as a senior technical leader responsible for developing and leading execution of the project data visualization strategy across the global management system (gms) and real-time visibility environment. this role owns technical direction for single-pane-of-glass dashboards, user experiences, visual analytics patterns, data products, reporting, alerting, and integration approaches that transform normalized, correlated, and enriched network, cyber, performance, configuration, event, and operational data into clear, reliable, actionable mission insights. the successful candidate will lead execution across a complex aws il5/il6 cloud-based system-of-systems that uses confluent kafka, elasticsearch, logstash, kibana, watson aiops, databricks, servicenow, palantir integration, network automation capabilities, and devsecops/ci/cd tooling. the role requires a strategic and flexible mindset to maximize existing program tools and investments while also defining the target-state architecture, roadmap, processes, standards, reusable patterns, development practices, and technology adoption path needed to take real-time visibility into the future. this is a senior technical leadership role for a candidate who can move fluidly between customer engagement, product strategy, architecture, data engineering, software development, ui/ux, visualization design, agile delivery, security, and operational transition. the rtv technical lead will work closely with product owners, the data driven operations manager, architects, data engineers, visualization engineers, software developers, ui/ux engineers, network engineers, cyber teams, operations users, vendors, and government stakeholders to define priorities, lead design and implementation, mentor team members, demonstrate capabilities, and deliver measurable mission and business value. primary responsibilities the successful candidate will: develop, maintain, and lead execution of the rtv data visualization strategy and roadmap across people, process, technology, tools, architecture, and implementation techniques. define current-state and target-state visualization architecture, information architecture, ux/ui patterns, dashboard standards, navigation models, design systems, accessibility expectations, and reusable components for elastic/kibana and adjacent visualization tools. lead the design, development, documentation, testing, deployment, and sustainment of kibana dashboards, visualizations, reports, alerts, self-service analytics, and operational data products that support real-time situational awareness and decision-making. maximize the use of existing program tools and investments, including elastic/kibana, elasticsearch, logstash, confluent kafka, watson aiops, databricks, servicenow, palantir, aws, jira, confluence, bitbucket, jenkins/cloudbees, artifactory, ansible, openshift/kubernetes, and related platform capabilities. evaluate new tools, custom development approaches, integration patterns, and modernization opportunities based on mission value, business value, user adoption, total cost of ownership, cybersecurity, operational supportability, performance, scalability, and technical fit. partner with data engineers and platform teams to ensure data pipelines deliver reliable visualization-ready data, influencing data normalization, correlation, enrichment, schema design, metadata, data contracts, lineage, quality rules, retention, and indexing strategies. collaborate with operational users, mission stakeholders, product owners, and subject matter experts to understand workflows, define outcomes, document requirements, create user journeys and personas, develop wireframes and prototypes, conduct demos, and incorporate feedback through iterative delivery. translate stakeholder needs into technical epics, user stories, acceptance criteria, design artifacts, implementation plans, test plans, user acceptance strategies, and operational transition plans. lead cross-functional agile execution, including technical backlog refinement, team capacity and workload prioritization, sprint planning support, design reviews, code reviews, testing strategy, release readiness, delivery risk management, and continuous improvement. establish and enforce dashboard and visual analytics governance, including standards, review processes, versioning, ownership, access controls, documentation, dashboard rationalization, lifecycle management, performance monitoring, and sustainment practices. design and guide implementation of visual analytics that support network operations, cyber operations, customer impact analysis, root cause analysis, service health, incident management, predictive insights, auto-ticketing, automated troubleshooting, and future self-healing network capabilities. integrate visualizations and decision products into operational workflows so they enable faster detect, troubleshoot, resolve, and report cycles, reduce false positives and false negatives, improve mean time to resolution, and support automated remediation where appropriate. develop and maintain technical artifacts, including architecture decision records, logical and physical visualization architectures, data flow diagrams, system design documents, interface documents, wireframes, dashboard catalogs, implementation plans, test strategies, and operational runbooks. ensure solutions comply with dod cybersecurity, data governance, role-based access control, encryption, auditability, privileged access, rmf, disa stig, and classified/unclassified environment requirements. troubleshoot and optimize dashboard query performance, data quality issues, indexing strategies, visualization load times, user experience issues, data pipeline dependencies, and platform performance constraints. brief program leadership, customers, and government stakeholders on visualization strategy, status, risks, tradeoffs, design decisions, demonstrations, roadmap options, and recommended courses of action. support engineering review board activities, technology trade studies, analysis of alternatives, rom and proposal inputs, roadmap planning, and modernization recommendations for new and enhanced gsm-o capabilities. maintain a forward-looking perspective on emerging data visualization, observability, ux/ui, ai/ml, aiops, llm-enabled operations support, automation, and network operations technologies, and recommend pragmatic adoption paths that improve mission outcomes. basic qualifications bachelor’s degree in computer science, data science, data engineering, software engineering, systems engineering, human-computer interaction, information systems, or a related technical discipline with 8+ years of relevant experience; master’s degree with 6+ years; or equivalent additional experience in lieu of degree. final experience requirement should be validated against the selected leidos job profile. demonstrated experience leading strategy, architecture, design, development, and delivery of data visualization, observability, analytics, or data-driven operations capabilities in complex enterprise or mission environments. hands-on experience designing, building, deploying, and sustaining operational dashboards, reports, visualizations, and data products using elastic/kibana or comparable enterprise visualization platforms. experience with the elastic stack, including elasticsearch, logstash, kibana, indexing strategies, dashboarding, alerting, role-based access, retention, observability, and performance tuning. experience with real-time or near-real-time operational data, such as network events, performance metrics, configuration data, telemetry, syslog, snmp polling/traps, incident/ticketing data, cybersecurity data, or customer impact data. experience translating mission, business, and user needs into technical requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, architecture/design artifacts, development tasks, and implementation plans. experience with user-centered design practices, including stakeholder interviews, workflow analysis, personas, user journeys, wireframes, prototypes, usability reviews, visual design principles, accessibility, and iterative feedback loops. experience leading technical teams or cross-functional delivery efforts, including mentoring engineers, influencing without direct authority, facilitating design decisions, resolving technical issues, managing delivery risk, and aligning execution to business outcomes. experience with data integration and pipeline concepts, including kafka or comparable messaging platforms, etl/elt, apis, data modeling, schema management, metadata, data quality, data lineage, and secure access patterns. software development or scripting experience using javascript, react, html, css, json/rest apis, python, java, sql, or comparable languages used for visualization, automation, platform integration, and data engineering. experience with devsecops and agile delivery practices, including git/bitbucket, jira, confluence, jenkins/cloudbees or equivalent ci/cd tooling, artifactory, ansible, automated testing, controlled release processes, and infrastructure/configuration as code concepts. experience with cloud and containerized environments such as aws, aws govcloud, openshift, kubernetes, docker, or comparable technologies. working knowledge of cybersecurity and compliance principles, including access controls, encryption, least privilege, auditability, rmf, disa stigs, dod ia policies, or comparable secure mission environment requirements. strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to brief technical solutions, tradeoffs, risks, status, and recommendations to customers, senior leadership, architects, engineers, operators, and non-technical stakeholders. ability to obtain and maintain a dod secret security clearance; active secret clearance preferred for start. ability to obtain security+ or equivalent dod 8570 iat ii certification within the program-required timeframe after start. preferred qualifications experience supporting disa, disn, dodin, gsm-o, gms, dod network operations, cyber operations, or mission command-and-control environments. deep understanding of network operations data and workflows, including service health, event correlation, topology, customer impact, incident management, root cause analysis, performance management, configuration management, and operational reporting. experience with tools or data sources such as dxnetops, netscout, netcool, watson aiops, syslog, snmp polling/traps, juniper northstar, ctpview, cisco epnm, ciena mcp, silvx, cisco prime optical, servicenow itsm/tsom/tni/omt, palantir, cisco nso, and ansible. elastic/kibana certification or demonstrated expert-level experience with elastic/kibana dashboard development, kibana lens, canvas, maps, alerting, spaces, security, saved objects, apis, custom plugins, or advanced visualization patterns. experience with confluent kafka or apache kafka, including topics, partitions, connectors, schema management, stream processing, kafka streams, ksqldb/ksql, and operational troubleshooting. experience with databricks, spark, delta lake, unity catalog or comparable data catalog/governance capabilities, apache nifi, apache flink, or similar data engineering technologies. experience designing visual analytics and operational data products that support predictive analytics, anomaly detection, aiops, event correlation, auto-ticketing, automated troubleshooting, automated remediation, or self-healing network capabilities. familiarity with ai/ml, nlp, llm-enabled operational support, elastic ai assistant or similar capabilities, feature engineering, model-ready data preparation, and governance of data used for machine learning workloads. experience optimizing elastic, kafka, cloud, or data visualization platforms for throughput, latency, query performance, storage lifecycle, high availability, resiliency, cost, and operational supportability. experience designing solutions that move, replicate, or consolidate data across security boundaries, including il5/il6 patterns, cross-domain transfer concepts, diode-based transfer patterns, and secure data consolidation. experience developing data visualization standards, reference architectures, reusable dashboard patterns, naming conventions, dashboard governance processes, and reusable ux components that accelerate delivery and improve enterprise consistency. experience with network fundamentals, routing and switching concepts, bgp, mpls, ip, optical networking, transport protocols, network device configurations, and network management systems. experience with engineering review boards, architecture governance, analysis of alternatives, trade title: Electrical Engineer, Sr.
body: leidos is seeking an experienced electrical engineer to join our antarctic support contract (asc) assigned to the facilities – engineering & design team, in support of the united states antarctic program. the electrical engineer will execute electrical designs ranging from small, single year projects to multi-year government projects in extreme winter environments for three (3) antarctic stations plus additional field camps. the antarctic support contract (asc) program team is based in centennial, colorado and funded by the united states national science foundation (nsf). the planning and implementation of science support requirements in antarctica is a critical part of our mission, and every team member plays a crucial role. ** this is a remote role but deployment to antarctica may be necessary at the discretion of management. ** successful completion of the physical and dental examinations required by the nsf for deploying to antarctica is a nonnegotiable requirement. ** due to contract requirements, us citizenship is required. ** must obtain a public trust security clearance prior to starting. this process could take up to 4 months. about the antarctic support contract leidos antarctic support contract (asc) is the prime contractor to the national science foundation (nsf) in support of the united states antarctic program (usap). leidos supports the nsf’s office of polar program’s antarctic infrastructure and logistics and provides science and logistics support for approximately 150 science and technical events across three geographically remote research stations; mcmurdo station, palmer station, and south pole station and several deep field sites across antarctica. each station or field site supports world class research across multiple science disciplines. to learn more about the leidos antarctic support contract, click here . responsibilities the electrical engineer is responsible for working as part of the body: leidos is currently seeking a safety engineer to support the antarctic support contract and the national science foundation's united states antarctic program. this position is remote with at least annual deployments within conus and to oconus locations with a focus on antarctic field, peninsula, and research vessel operations. responsible for administering and implementing occupational safety, health, and risk management strategies in field camp locations and operations that are peripheral to antarctic stations. this position deploys frequently to antarctic station and field environment and acts as the primary safety point of contact (poc) for projects and operations that occur in the station and field region(s). additionally, this position works in the off-season to assess, develop, and implement risk management strategies and plans, participates in pre-season science, and sustain operations reviews and planning meetings. *this is an alternate position for the austral summer season. deployment location is mcmurdo station, antarctica. must be able to obtain a public trust clearance. this process may take up to 4 months. responsibilities include: ensures station, field and peripheral operations meet safety and health program requirements and assists managers with the integration of key standards and use of risk management to prevent injuries in the usap operational environment. ensures that asc operations align with current health and safety standards, and, where applicable, conforms to federal regulations. employee must be able to act with leadership from a safety and risk management perspective at field camps and peripheral operations. follows-up and provides assistance with incident investigations and root cause analysis. performs industrial hygiene and safety surveys. documents findings according to accepted procedures. uses and maintains health and safety related instrumentation, including 4-gas meters, noise dosimeters, respiratory quantafit, and photo ionization detectors. provides technical reports on improvement strategies plan/project status to h&s manager. assists other members of the ehs team with analysis, report generations, and project completion in the standard occupational station and filed environments. required qualifications: bs in safety sciences, chemistry, environmental, engineering, or related field is required. equivalent relevant experience may be accepted in lieu of a degree. minimum of 5 years experience with safety and health rules, regulations, standards, and the components of an effective safety program, including plant operations and/or construction safety, fire protection, public health, and development of related training programs is required. field experience with logistic base support for remote work camps with emphasis on heavy industrial or construction environments. be able to adapt to extreme weather conditions such as high winds, low temperatures. excellent written and oral communications. individuals may achieve varying levels of professional certification in safety and/or industrial hygiene or equivalent through continuing education and experience. preferred qualifications: relevant antarctic or arctic esh experience is preferred. professional certification as a certified safety professional (csp) certified industrial hygienist (cih) title: Principal Systems Engineer Air Traffic Management
body: leidos is seeking a principal systems engineer with strong air traffic control (atc) domain experience, with particular emphasis on oceanic and en route air traffic operations and systems. this is an opportunity to bring deep operational and technical expertise to programs that are shaping the future of air traffic management, helping evolve the systems and capabilities that will support increasingly modern, connected, and efficient airspace operations. the principal systems engineer will join a dynamic team supporting the air traffic division under homeland having opportunities to contribute to domestic and international air traffic management initiatives. the successful candidate will help define and advance the next generation of mission-critical air traffic management (atm) capabilities, applying lessons learned from today's operational environments to the systems that will support the future of aviation and global airspace operations. this role is ideal for someone who assignment actions for primary surveillance radar systems, air-to-ground voice communication, land mobile radio, microwave, satellite, and various other radio frequency (rf) spectrum engineering disciplines while ensuring compliance with faa order 6050.32 and ntia redbook requirements. core responsibilities (all bands): contributes to the planning, coordination, and execution of faa and program offices to resolve technical issues and advance records through the assignment and coordination process. basic qualifications: bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering or completion of a support the national airspace system (nas). experience in applying analytical and automation tools to perform frequency-assignment processing, data validation, and compatibility analysis, with attention to accuracy and completeness. experience evaluating radio-frequency system parameters to identify and mitigate potential interference and resolving routine and complex spectrum-engineering problems. familiar with spectrum xxi or similar federal spectrum management tools is highly desirable . ability to perform engineering calculations (fspl, link budgets, noise/interference ratios, power conversions). ability to interpret technical data and apply mitigation best practices to resolve rf interference issues affecting aviation systems. knowledge of roles and responsibilities of spectrum management within the national airspace system (nas). knowledge of frequency management practices, including engineering, assignment, and protection of radio frequencies, and the national title: DDI Architect
body: needed: ddi architect (dns / dhcp / ipam) – nasa about the role nasa seeks a seasoned ddi architect to lead the architecture, design, engineering, and lifecycle management of enterprise-scale dns, dhcp, and ip address management (ipam) services across corporate and mission networks. the role will drive secure, resilient name resolution aligned to federal requirements—including nist sp 800‑53 controls for secure name/address resolution (sc‑20, sc‑21) , nist sp 800‑81r3 dns security guidance , and cisa encrypted/protective dns mandates —and support nasa’s mission-critical dns operations, which include participation as a root server operator (e‑root) . you will partner closely with engineering, system administration, and operations teams. key responsibilities: enterprise ddi architecture & compliance design and maintain authoritative and recursive dns architectures that implement nist sp 800‑53 sc‑20 (authoritative) and sc‑21 (recursive/caching) —including dnssec signing/validation and chain-of-trust with ds records. operationalize nist sp 800‑81r3 guidance for secure dns deployment (protective dns, encrypted dns protocols such as dot/doh/doq, logging/forensics, qname minimization) across enterprise dns roles (authoritative servers, resolvers, zone administration). ensure compliance with cisa’s encrypted dns implementation guidance and zero trust objectives, including routing egress resolution via cisa protective dns (pdns) and blocking unauthorized external resolvers. align with cisa binding operational directives (bods) — bod 18‑01 (dmarc/hsts/starttls), bod 22‑01 (kev remediation timelines), bod 23‑01 (asset visibility/vulnerability detection), and bod 23‑02 (mitigate internet‑exposed management interfaces). drive ipv6‑first strategy per omb m‑21‑07 (native ipv6 for public services, ipv6‑only milestones) and maintain dual‑stack transition hygiene for dns, dhcpv6, and ipam. operations, risk reduction & lifecycle management serve as technical lead for large‑scale ddi environments, overseeing secure configurations, automation, availability, and performance across centers. (role scope mirrors enterprise‑class environments consistent with nasa’s operational scale.) implement protective controls and monitoring to detect, log, and investigate dns misuse; integrate with siem/soar for forensics and incident response per 800‑81r3. maintain continuous vulnerability management aligned to cisa’s kev catalog and reporting expectations; coordinate remediation timelines and control validation. secure networked management interfaces (e.g., dns appliance ui/api, dhcp consoles, ipam admin) by removing public exposure or enforcing zero trust policy enforcement points in accordance with bod 23‑02 . govern dns email‑related configurations (spf/dkim/dmarc) to meet bod 18‑01 requirements and support nasa email architecture. root & .gov domain stewardship participate in operations for e.root‑servers.org (e‑root) as applicable—supporting authoritative root zone service, anycast deployments, and adherence to rssac‑002 metrics and rso coordination. ensure .gov domain compliance (dnssec signing, secure delegation) per federal directives and nist guidance. ip address governance administer top‑level allocations and growth planning for ipv4/ipv6 , consistent with arin policies and best practices (aggregation, rpki, reverse dns hygiene). automation & modernization evaluate and integrate ddi platform capabilities (e.g., encrypted dns with pdns, dnssec automation, dhcpv6 prefix delegation, ipam apis), and champion modernization aligned with zero trust and federal cdm initiatives. minimum qualifications: bachelor's degree and 10+ years of experience, or an associate's degree and 15+ years of experience designing and operating enterprise dns/dhcp/ipam (ddi) services, with demonstrated authority in secure dns architectures (dnssec, validating resolvers, signed zones, ds management). (aligned to nist sp 800‑53 sc‑20/sc‑21.) hands‑on implementation of nist sp 800‑81r3 practices: protective dns, encrypted dns (dot/doh/doq), secure recursive resolvers, authoritative hardening, and comprehensive dns logging/forensics. practical experience meeting cisa’s encrypted dns guidance and pdns integration; ability to prevent unauthorized dns traffic and enforce endpoint, cloud, and sase/sse dns policies. proven track record implementing federal bods (18‑01, 22‑01, 23‑01, 23‑02) within large environments, including kev‑driven patch prioritization and zero trust controls for management interfaces. ipv6 expertise: dns over ipv6, dhcpv6, ipam for ipv6, and strategic migration compliant with omb m‑21‑07 milestones. familiarity with .gov dnssec requirements and secure delegation processes for federal domains. knowledge of arin policies (nrpm), address planning/aggregation, and registry hygiene (whois/poc validation, rpki, reverse dns). ​ preferred qualifications: experience supporting or coordinating with root server operators ; familiarity with e‑root anycast operations and rssac‑002 metrics submissions. prior leadership in environments with protective dns and encrypted dns end‑to‑end (endpoint, internal resolvers, egress to pdns, cloud). demonstrated capability to manage dmarc/spf/dkim deployments at scale per bod 18‑01 (including hsts/https and starttls hardening). experience integrating ddi with asset discovery and vulnerability enumeration programs per bod 23‑01 ; evidence of kev remediation workflows. strong understanding of nist sp 800‑53 rev.5 broader control families (sc, si, au) and mapping to dns/network operations. background with arin ipv6 allocations, asn operations, and address governance at federal scale. clearance requirements: u.s. citizenship is required. ability to obtain and maintain a public trust. if you're looking for comfort, keep scrolling. at leidos, we outthink, outbuild, and outpace the status quo — because the mission demands it. we're not hiring followers. we're recruiting the ones who disrupt, provoke, and refuse to fail. step 10 is ancient history. we're already at step 30 — and moving faster than anyone else dares. original posting: august 7, 2026 for u.s. positions: while subject to change based on business needs, leidos reasonably anticipates that this job requisition will remain open for at least 3 days with an anticipated close date of no earlier than 3 days after the original posting date as listed above. pay range: pay range $92,300.00 - $166,850.00 the leidos pay range for this job level is a general guideline only and not a guarantee of compensation or salary. additional factors considered in extending an offer include (but are not limited to) responsibilities of the job, education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity, alignment with market data, applicable bargaining agreement (if any), or other law.

devops, infrastructure, systems, and product teams. the role translates cybersecurity standards, customer requirements, and product risk into practical controls across architecture, software development, ci/cd pipelines, and the shared deployment platform. the engineer will develop reusable security tooling, automation, hardened configurations, and technical documentation; assess and supporting dhs and tsa. in this role, you’ll work collaboratively to maintain and operate the program’s environments. position will be responsible for installing, supporting, and maintaining red hat openshift and mas 9 implementations and will help automate and streamline our operations and processes, troubleshoot and resolve issues in our dev, test and production environments, gather user requirements and document functional and technical specifications, create thorough system documentation, and support team members and end users with both technical expertise and training. this position utilizes in-depth knowledge of openshift and mas 9 best practices and their own experience to provide and improve services. this position will work independently and is expected to be able to operate with minimal guidance. necessary skills include software and systems development, test and evaluation, configuration and release management, data management, it security, service desk, operations and maintenance functions, and supporting business process engineering services for the portfolio. this position is remote so the successful candidate will be able to work in that environment. primary responsibilities: work as part of team to provide evaluation of system requirements, architectures, models, designs and release/deployment plans. assess the operational and functional baselines and its supporting systems. document system architecture and associated designs by analyzing requirements; constructing workflow charts and diagrams; studying system capabilities; writing specifications. help develop and improve standards for application development and maintenance. prepare technical reports by collecting, analyzing and summarizing information and trends. implement practical lifecycle system engineering practices for maximo application suite and supporting openshift and oracle infrastructure. mas security: ensure that mas 9 is designed and operates so as to meet all of the security requirements necessary to obtain and retain a dhs authority to operate. work as part of a team to administer maximo in a high availability high security environment. maintain system protocols, architecture, requirements and associated design documents by enforcing traceability, updating procedures, analyzing system and program changes support configuration management, quality assurance, and cybersecurity throughout the release cycle in a devsecops environment. participate in the development of action plans to remedy findings from security assessments, work with system development teams to remediate findings and when required provide solutions to system teams. mas operations and maintenance: install, configure, support, and maintain mas 9 and the red hat openshift and oracle (enterprise/standard databases) infrastructure that underpin the mas 9 environment. achieve required performance measures as defined in program service level agreements and statements of work. plan and implement maintenance activities, including patches, hotfixes, and upgrades. resolve problems reported or discovered, including root cause analysis, problem remediation, and reporting. develop reports using maximo business intelligence reporting (birt) and cognos analytics. provide system training to end users/system owners assist in it service desk and troubleshooting to quickly resolve issues for end users including direct support via telephone. mas enhancements: gather business requirements, perform software development, system testing and implementation of ibm maximo software components and modules. gather and document user requirements and functional/technical specifications for software solutions. identify enhancements or improvements to systems by studying current workflows and designs and determining inefficiencies. schedule, plan, implement, and test enhancements and improvements to maximo systems. support implementation of new functionality in maximo including version upgrades and addition of new modules. develop and troubleshoot integrations in maximo integration framework to integrate key enterprise-wide systems basic qualifications: candidate must be a us citizen and able to obtain dhs or tsa vetting (active preferred). bachelor’s degree from an accredited college in a related discipline, or equivalent experience/combined education, with 10-15 years of professional experience. direct experience may substitute for years of education on a one for one basis. ability to work as part of an integrated team while remaining self-disciplined on task execution. strong focus on the mission including direct customer support. experience and expertise in the following operating systems and other cots products: ibm products : red hat open shift, maximo application suite 9, redhat enterprise linux, cognos, maximo integration framework oracle enterprise and standard databases aws infrastructure and platform service offerings (vpc, ec2, ebs, elb, s3, and rds. (aws certification a plus) solid written and verbal communication skills. ability to adjust schedule to meet program needs. some evening, weekend work will be required. experience in a fedramp (or other secured cloud) environment is required. experience implementing and maintaining a high security it environment is required. experience installing, supporting, and maintaining ibm maximo application suite is required. experience installing, supporting, and maintaining red hat openshift is required. tsa suitability determination preferred qualifications: experience installing, supporting, and maintaining oracle (enterprise and standard databases). participation in app development for mobile and desktop environments experience with mobile app development existing public trust or security clearance experience with aws if you're looking for comfort, keep scrolling. at leidos, we outthink, outbuild, and outpace the status quo — because the mission demands it. we're not hiring followers. we're recruiting the ones who disrupt, provoke, and refuse to fail. step 10 is ancient history. we're already at step 30 — and moving faster than anyone else dares. original posting: august 3, 2026 for u.s. positions: while subject to change based on business needs, leidos reasonably anticipates that this job requisition will remain open for at least 3 days with an anticipated close date of no earlier than 3 days after the original posting date as listed above. pay range: pay range $116,350.00 - $210,325.00 the leidos pay range for this job level is a general guideline only and not a guarantee of compensation or salary. additional factors considered in extending an offer include (but are not limited to) responsibilities of the job, education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity, alignment with market data, applicable bargaining agreement (if any), or other law.

title: Security Architecture & Engineering Lead
body: the force protection division is seeking a security architecture & engineering lead to serve as the cybersecurity technical authority for the integration, accreditation, testing, and operational assessment of force protection sensing technologies supporting the rock island arsenal (ria) increased access ota prototype. the successful candidate will lead the development and execution of the program's cybersecurity strategy, ensuring the prototype is securely integrated into existing department of defense (dod) network environments and achieves the required cybersecurity authorizations to support operational testing and transition. the security architecture & engineering lead is responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing all cybersecurity engineering activities throughout the prototype lifecycle, including security architecture development, risk management framework (rmf) implementation, security technical implementation guide (stig) compliance, assured compliance assessment solution (acas) vulnerability management, and development of accreditation artifacts supporting an interim authority to test (iatt), interim authority to operate (iato), and ultimately an authorization to operate (ato). the individual will serve as the program's primary cybersecurity engineering lead, ensuring cybersecurity requirements are integrated into system design, development, integration, verification, and operational validation activities. working closely with government stakeholders, leidos engineering teams, subcontractors, and commercial technology providers, the security architecture & engineering lead will oversee the secure integration of multiple vendor solutions into an existing dod enterprise environment. the individual will identify and mitigate cybersecurity risks associated with integrating commercial off-the-shelf (cots), government off-the-shelf (gots), and prototype technologies while ensuring compliance with dod cybersecurity policies, army security requirements, and applicable federal standards. the security architecture & engineering lead collaborates across systems engineering, software engineering, networking, integration and test, and program management organizations to resolve technical issues, manage cybersecurity risks, support operational assessments, and enable the successful fielding of a secure, mission-ready prototype. the position requires a technically proficient cybersecurity leader capable of balancing mission execution, engineering rigor, and operational objectives within a fast-paced prototype development environment. primary responsibilities develop the cybersecurity integration strategy for incorporating multiple oem sensing technologies into the ria increased access prototype while balancing mission effectiveness, interoperability, operational usability, and cybersecurity compliance within the existing rock island arsenal enterprise environment. basic qualifications bachelor’s degree and 8 – 12 years of prior relevant experience. demonstrated experience leading security architecture and engineering activities throughout the system development life cycle (sdlc) for complex department of defense (dod) systems.. demonstrated experience developing and implementing cybersecurity architectures that support the integration of multiple hardware, software, networking, and operational technology (ot) components into existing dod enterprise or tactical network environments.. demonstrated experience planning and executing the risk management framework (rmf) process, including development of rmf artifacts required to obtain an interim authority to test (iatt), interim authority to operate (iato), and/or authorization to operate (ato). demonstrated experience developing, maintaining, and managing rmf documentation and artifacts, including system security plans (ssps), security assessment plans (saps), security assessment reports (sars), plans of action & milestones (poa&ms), emass packages, and supporting accreditation documentation. demonstrated experience developing, reviewing, and implementing security technical implementation guides (stigs), assured compliance assessment solution (acas) scanning requirements, vulnerability remediation plans, and security compliance documentation for dod information systems. demonstrated experience identifying, assessing, and mitigating cybersecurity risks associated with integrating multiple commercial, government, and third-party vendor systems into existing dod network environments. demonstrated experience leading technical integration efforts involving multiple engineering disciplines, subcontractors, vendors, and government stakeholders while ensuring compliance with dod cybersecurity policies, rmf requirements, and accreditation objectives. demonstrated experience executing systems engineering activities including technical planning, system architecture, technical design, development, integration, verification, validation, and transition to operational use. demonstrated experience designing, engineering, implementing, integrating, maintaining, and continuously improving secure hardware, software, communications, and infrastructure components supporting mission-critical systems. demonstrated experience serving as the cybersecurity engineering lead or technical authority responsible for security accreditation activities supporting operational assessments, developmental testing, field demonstrations, or system deployment. preferred qualifications experience obtaining iatts or iatos for prototype systems supporting operational assessments, user evaluations, or developmental testing. experience supporting army, joint, or other dod rapid prototyping and capability demonstration efforts. experience integrating commercial off-the-shelf (cots), government off-the-shelf (gots), and third-party vendor technologies into accredited dod environments. experience with zero trust architecture, devsecops, continuous ato, and cloud-enabled security architectures. professional cybersecurity certifications such as cissp, casp+, security+, title: Senior Supply Chain Risk Management Threat Intelligence Lead Analyst
body: leidos is seeking a senior supply chain risk management threat intelligence lead analyst to provide advanced, high-level technical and analytical support to the faa’s counterintelligence (ci) supply chain risk management (scrm) program. the program is responsible for identifying, assessing, and mitigating foreign intelligence, nation-state, and cybersecurity threats to the faa’s supply chain, critical infrastructure, and enterprise networks. embedded as a senior analyst within a 4-person team, this position focuses on threat landscapes, adversarial intent, and geopolitical vulnerability modeling. providing independent, authoritative all-source intelligence analysis, the senior analyst designs analytic methodologies using open source intelligence (osint) and corporate registries to uncover hidden foreign ownership, control, or influence (foci), technology transfer risks, and strategic threat trends targeting the aviation industrial base. this role oversees the evaluation of physical, technical, and personnel vulnerabilities, including sophisticated hardware/firmware threats and insider risks, to produce exquisite intelligence briefings that guide faa executive leadership and empower the broader scrm framework. primary responsibilities: ensure strict quality control, mentoring, and analytical integrity across all faa ci scrm products. conduct proactive threat analysis of foreign suppliers, third-party software developers, and hardware manufacturers to identify nation-state activity and strategic threat trends targeting the faa. utilize osint and corporate registries to screen prospective faa vendors and evaluate the supply chain for foreign ownership, control, or influence (foci) indicators, foreign partnerships, and technology transfer threats. monitor specialized threat feeds, nation-state activities, and geopolitical shifts to identify, evaluate, and mitigate strategic supply chain risks to the faa. support the faa insider risk program by identifying and analyzing personnel concerns, anomalous vendor behaviors, and internal vulnerabilities. evaluate threat vectors including malicious hardware or software modifications, supply chain transit interdiction, and counterfeit electronic components. synthesize complex data to produce clear, actionable supplier threat profiles, country risk profiles, link-analysis diagrams, and timely threat alerts/advisories for faa program managers, technical teams, and executive decision-makers. translate highly complex counterintelligence findings, technical hardware/software vulnerabilities, and macroeconomic geopolitical risks into exquisite intelligence briefings, dashboards, and executive decision packages tailored specifically for senior faa leadership. formulate performance metrics and program reports for executive leadership. maintain critical operational and collaborative relationships with external stakeholders, including the faa chief information officer (cio), cybersecurity and infrastructure security agency (cisa), federal bureau of investigation (fbi), department of homeland security (dhs), and the broader intelligence community (ic). coordinate and facilitate scrm training and awareness campaigns for acquisition personnel and program offices. basic qualifications: citizenship: u.s. citizenship required. clearance: active top secret/sci clearance is required. education: bachelor’s or master’s degree in supply chain, intelligence studies, national security, logistics, data science, cybersecurity, information technology, computer science, computer engineering, or a related technical discipline. (equivalent professional experience or specialized military/federal training may be substituted). experience: 12+ years of professional experience as an intelligence analyst (all-source, cyber, counterintelligence, or open-source intelligence) or senior-level experience in third-party risk management (tprm), cyber supply chain risk management (c-scrm), technical risk assessments, it auditing, cybersecurity risk management, or infrastructure defense in a federal or highly regulated commercial environment. analytical capability: proven experience using corporate registries, commercial databases, and osint techniques to analyze corporate structures, trace components, and evaluate foci. technical skills: proficiency with due diligence or corporate intelligence platforms (e.g., sayari, altana, interos, maltego) and/or data modeling. communication skills: exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with a proven track record of translating complex intelligence and technical risk data into clear, concise executive briefs and formal written reports for non-technical stakeholders and delivering briefing materials to c-suite or flag-level leadership. preferred qualifications: completion of formal military or federal intelligence training courses focusing on threat network analysis or open-source collection. high proficiency with advanced osint search techniques, corporate filing retrieval systems, and international trade/shipping databases. familiarity with the acquisition frameworks and an understanding of how supply chain intelligence feeds into federal procurement lifecycles. prior experience supporting threat intelligence or counterintelligence infrastructure defense missions specifically for critical infrastructure or a federal agency. if defense. framework knowledge: strong working knowledge of federal cybersecurity and risk management frameworks, specifically nist sp 800-161 (cybersecurity supply chain risk management practices) and title: Field Engineer 3
body: as one of leidos’ oldest and largest programs supporting the federal aviation administration (faa), the nas integration support contract (nisc) program is seeking a qualified professional to support the faa’s brand-new air traffic control system (bnatcs) initiative—specifically the radar surveillance replacement (rsr) program office (ajm-41)—by serving as an rsr field engineer on the program office’s implementation and disposition teams. the selected candidate will support installation and disposition for the rsr po, at some of the nation’s busiest and most critical airports. primary responsibilities represent the po at rsr sites, executing to an aggressive multi-site schedule. serve as an rsr subject matter expert (sme) to the rsr program office project, implementation, operational risk management practices. ability to perform at a high level independently and as part of a small team, while meeting an aggressive installation schedule. demonstrated commitment to title: Supply Chain Risk Management Specialist
body: leidos is seeking a supply chain risk management analyst to provide technical and analytical support to the federal aviation administration's (faa) counterintelligence (ci) supply chain risk management (scrm) program. the program is responsible for identifying, assessing, and mitigating foreign intelligence, nation-state, and cybersecurity threats to the faa’s supply chain, critical infrastructure, and enterprise networks. embedded within a 3-person team, this position focuses on enterprise risk assessments and procurement execution support. providing risk analysis aligned with the faa acquisition management system (ams) framework, the analyst evaluates the actual security posture of software suppliers, cloud providers, artificial intelligence (ai) tools, telecommunications, and operational technology / industrial control systems (ot/ics) environments. this role translates threat data into technical risk scoring, conducts criticality analysis, and drafts custom contract security language to protect and mitigate threats against faa supply chain. primary responsibilities: conduct enterprise-level vendor risk assessments and technical security reviews for software suppliers, cloud providers (saas/paas/iaas), ai tools, telecommunications, and ot/ics (operational technology/industrial control systems). conduct technical and non-technical risk scoring to compile comprehensive vendor risk reports that map systemic vulnerabilities. provide specialized scrm subject matter expertise throughout the procurement lifecycle, including early-stage acquisition planning and source selections. author acquisition security reviews and evaluation matrices that integrate directly into the faa acquisition management system (ams) pipeline. draft specific contract security language, technical security requirements, and risk acceptance recommendations to mitigate identified supply chain risks prior to contract award. translate highly technical and complex risk assessment data into clear, executive decision packages for a non-technical audience to enable faa senior leadership to make rapid, fully informed decisions. contribute to the development and maintenance of faa scrm policies, governance documentation, and standard operating procedures (sops). formulate performance metrics and program reports for executive leadership. maintain critical operational and collaborative relationships with external stakeholders, including the faa chief information officer (cio), cybersecurity and infrastructure security agency (cisa), federal bureau of investigation (fbi), department of homeland security (dhs), and the broader intelligence community (ic). coordinate and facilitate scrm training and awareness campaigns for acquisition personnel and program offices. basic qualifications: citizenship: u.s. citizenship required clearance: active top secret/sci clearance is required education: bachelor’s degree in supply chain risk management, intelligence studies, national security, logistics, data science, cybersecurity, information technology, computer science/engineering, or a related discipline. (equivalent professional experience or specialized training may be substituted). experience: 8+ years of professional experience as an intelligence analyst (all-source, cyber, counterintelligence, or osint) or professional experience in third-party risk management (tprm), cyber supply chain risk management (c-scrm), technical risk assessments, cybersecurity risk management, or infrastructure defense. framework knowledge: strong working knowledge of federal cybersecurity and risk management frameworks, specifically nist sp 800-161 (cybersecurity supply chain risk management practices) and nist sp 800-53. technical skills: hands-on experience evaluating the security posture, software supply chains, and configurations of at least three of the following technology profiles: cloud infrastructure and service providers (saas, paas, iaas) commercial software packages and open-source dependencies artificial intelligence (ai) platforms or machine learning tools telecommunications hardware or infrastructure frameworks operational technology (ot) or industrial control systems (ics) communication skills: proven capability to translate complex technical vulnerabilities, software flaws, and architectural risks into clear, well-structured, non-technical written reports and executive summaries. preferred qualifications: completion of formal military or federal intelligence training courses focusing on threat network analysis or open-source collection. possession of one or more of the following industry-recognized certifications: certified information systems security professional (cissp) certified in risk and information systems control (crisc) certified information systems auditor (cisa) specialized federal scrm or counterintelligence training certifications (e.g., cdse, odni, or defense-sponsored scrm courses). proficiency with advanced osint search techniques, corporate filing retrieval systems, or international trade/shipping databases. demonstrated title: Senior Electrical Engineer/Radio Frequency (RF) Engineer
body: leidos’ nisc iv program seeks an electrical engineer/ radio frequency (rf) engineer to support the federal aviation administration (faa) spectrum engineering services group. the spectrum engineering group is responsible for securing, managing, and protecting all civil aviation spectrum resources to ensure interference-free operation of faa communications, navigation, and surveillance (cns) systems across the national airspace system (nas). the candidate will be responsible for supporting the investigation, analysis, and resolution of radio frequency (rf) interference affecting critical communications, navigation, and surveillance systems. the ideal candidate will have strong experience in rf spectrum analysis, interference mitigation, radio direction finding, and field investigations using industry-standard test equipment. primary responsibilities rf interference investigation investigate reports of radio frequency interference (rfi) affecting mission-critical communications, navigation, surveillance, or wireless systems. perform both on-site and remote rf interference investigations to identify, characterize, and resolve interference sources. conduct root-cause analysis of intermittent and persistent rf interference events. document findings, recommend corrective actions, and verify successful mitigation of interference issues. spectrum analysis operate spectrum analyzers, monitoring receivers, and related rf test equipment to identify interfering emissions. measure and analyze: frequency bandwidth occupied spectrum modulation characteristics power levels harmonics spurious emissions evaluate rf propagation characteristics, signal strength, noise floor, and overall spectrum utilization. interpret rf measurements and prepare technical reports for engineering and operational stakeholders. radio direction finding (rdf) perform radio direction finding (rdf/df) operations to locate unknown rf interference sources. utilize directional antennas, gps mapping, and triangulation techniques during field investigations. conduct drive testing and field measurements to accurately pinpoint interference locations. support rapid response activities for high-priority interference events. required qualifications bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, telecommunications, computer engineering, or a related technical field (or equivalent experience). minimum 8+ years of experience in rf engineering, spectrum management, interference mitigation, or wireless communications. experience conducting rf interference investigations and root-cause analysis. proficiency using rf test equipment, including: spectrum analyzers monitoring receivers signal generators rf power meters experience with radio direction finding equipment and techniques. understanding of rf propagation, antenna theory, modulation methods, and electromagnetic interference (emi). ability to analyze technical data and prepare detailed engineering reports. strong troubleshooting and analytical skills. willingness to travel for field investigations as required. excellent troubleshooting and problem-solving abilities. strong written and verbal communication skills. ability to work independently and collaboratively in field and office environments. experience working in fast-paced operational environments. strong attention to detail and commitment to technical excellence. valid driver's license. must be a us citizen. preferred qualifications experience supporting aviation, public safety, defense, telecommunications, or government communications systems. familiarity with fcc, ntia, or international spectrum regulations. experience with spectrum monitoring software and gis/gps mapping applications. knowledge of digital title: Peninsula Field Camp Assistant
body: the united states antarctic program has an opening for a field camp assistant supporting national science foundation-funded field science on the antarctic peninsula. this a dynamic position working in remote locations to prepare for and assist camp operations for field scientists .this is a contractual position, physically strenuous for short and intense bursts. the candidate must be able to deploy to remote locations: either our cargo hub of punta arenas, chile, or via usap support vessels to areas along the antarctic peninsula for day trips or multi-day camping. the person in this position must have an active resume leading remote camping groups, be capable of lifting up to 35lbs, and pass a national security background check. in the event of funded nsf funded science field groups: willing and able to pass medical pre-qualification process. primary responsibilities: travel to punta arenas chile for 3 weeks each/ twice a year (oct/nov and again april/may) to perform the following functions: organize, prep and pack expedition gear for day trips up to multi-week camping trips in antarctic conditions . assist with cargo movements including packaging, labeling, weighing, and palletizing, as well as lifting, hauling and carrying and securing. assist with routine end-of-season cleaning and maintenance of camp equipment. maintain and repair camping and mountaineering gear at end of season in-shop or complete field-repairs in-situ as needed. help guide, train and work worth scientists of varying levels of camping and outdoor experience on safe field practices and usap procedures. in the event of funded science expeditions in outyears 2027/28, 28/29. be able to lead a full camp set-up/take-down including: moving cargo, setting up tents, cooking station, waste station, fueling areas, medical area, etc. according to usap standards. assist with daily camp chores to maintain a safe, healthy and hygienic environment including: waste sorting and management according to environmental standards, haul or melt snow for water, cook meals, dish washing and galley duties, charge communications devices, etc. may operate snow machines, atv’s, generators and other small machinery. familiarity and ability to perform daily communications check-ins via a variety of devices/methods: iridium, hf radio, vfh radio, starlink. assist with moving and carrying scientific samples as needed. maintain a positive work environment in order to achieve a safe scientific expedition. basic qualifications: high school diploma or ged two years of combined experience is required in any of the following areas: expedition outfitting in polar climates or high altitude winter settings, national park service positions, outdoor education, and/or guiding services. familiarity with working on or maintaining field camp gear. experience working on or from ships, sea kayaking, sailing or other maritime pursuits. basic navigational skills and able to operate a gps. wilderness first responder certification. preferred qualifications: bachelors degree in science: geology, marine, biology, ecology. experience with operating and maintenance of engines: atv and snow machines, generators. commercial sewing skills. backpacking, climbing and mountaineering particularly in high latitude or polar climates. vessel experience: sailing, small boats, commercial, or research. spanish language skills or proficiency. experience with outward bound, nols or another outdoor leadership school. w-emt or equivalent. *** deployment to antarctica may be
